## C) Combine {#sec-gpp-combine}

Both finished, independent products exist by this point -- A)'s `monthly_gpp_rast`, B)'s `pml_gpp_rast`. Everything below just combines them: resample NASA's record onto PML's own coarser grid, bias-check and pixel-scale correct PML against it (the same `compare_gpp_rasters()`/`build_gpp_pixel_ratio_raster()`/`apply_gpp_pixel_ratio_correction()` functions A) already used, shown in full in iii.-iv. above -- not repeated here), then splice corrected PML in underneath NASA's own record. PML only ever extends the record backwards (1982-1999, the one stretch neither MODIS nor VIIRS reaches) -- `combine_spatraster_list()`'s own priority ordering means PML's corrected values are only used where NASA has nothing, with no manual pre-trim needed.

### ix. Bias-check, correct and splice in PML

`resample_to_grid()` first coarsens NASA's native-500m monthly record onto PML's 0.1 degree grid (an area-weighted average, not point resampling), so the two sides of the comparison that follows are on the same grid. The bias-check and correction then run exactly the same way A)'s own NASA-internal ones did (iii.-iv. above), just with PML/NASA in place of MOD17/VIIRS. See @fig-agreement-by-month (row c) and @fig-pixel-ratio-maps (panels g-i), in [Correction and Splice Diagnostics](#sec-gpp-figures) at the end of this document.

#### Code

```{r}
#| label: src-targets-step-ix
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| code-summary: "_targets.R -- ix. Bias-check, correct and splice in PML"

  # ix. Bias-check, correct and splice in PML -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Both finished, independent products (A's monthly_gpp_rast, B's pml_gpp_rast) exist by this point -- everything below just combines them. PML only ever extends the record backwards (1982-1999, the one stretch neither MODIS nor VIIRS reaches) -- see combine_spatraster_list()'s own header for how the merge below only uses PML's own corrected values where NASA genuinely has nothing, with no manual pre-trim needed.

  # Resample NASA's finished record onto the standard covariate grid (section 1's own covariate_grid_template, not pml_gpp_rast directly -- see that target's own comment) -- PML's own comparison/correction reference.
  tar_terra_rast(monthly_gpp_rast_coarse, resample_to_grid(monthly_gpp_rast, covariate_grid_template), gdal = covariate_gdal_options),

  # Diagnostic: how well PML and this pipeline's own (corrected) NASA record agree, over their full 1982-2020 overlap. rast_a = our own record, rast_b = PML -- positive bias_mean means PML reads higher.
  gpp_pml_bias_check = compare_gpp_rasters(monthly_gpp_rast_coarse, pml_gpp_rast, structured_survey_points),

  # Pixel-scale ratio correction for PML. See r/b_build_gpp_pixel_ratio_raster.R for the correction itself.
  tar_terra_rast(gpp_pml_pixel_ratio_rast, build_gpp_pixel_ratio_raster(monthly_gpp_rast_coarse, pml_gpp_rast), gdal = covariate_gdal_options),

  # Corrected PML, full 1982-2020 range -- only its pre-2000 portion ever ends up in the merged record below (NASA is used automatically for 2000+, where both cover a period), so no separate pre-2000 trim is needed -- see combine_spatraster_list()'s own header for why.
  tar_terra_rast(pml_gpp_rast_corrected, apply_gpp_pixel_ratio_correction(pml_gpp_rast, gpp_pml_pixel_ratio_rast), gdal = covariate_gdal_options),

  # Merge corrected PML in underneath NASA's own record (NASA listed first/priority, PML the fallback for 1982-1999) -- the final, continuous 1982+ product every downstream covariate below is built from.
  # pml_gpp_rast_corrected is already cropped to covariate_download_region (+ margin, viii. above), while resample_to_grid() crops monthly_gpp_rast_coarse down to covariate_download_region's own (slightly different) footprint -- crop the former to the latter's exact extent here so the merge sees two same-extent stacks, not just two similarly-sized ones.
  tar_terra_rast(
    gpp_raster_coarse,
    combine_spatraster_list(list(monthly_gpp_rast_coarse, terra::crop(pml_gpp_rast_corrected, monthly_gpp_rast_coarse))),
    preserve_metadata = "zip",
    gdal              = covariate_gdal_options
  ),

```

### x. National + paddock mean diagnostics {#sec-gpp-national-paddock}

I build every figure in this report from one shared helper I wrote, `raster_mean_series()` -- it collapses a SpatRaster to a tidy one-row-per-layer mean, either nationally or at a fixed set of points (structured-survey paddocks, when `points` is supplied). My report's own setup chunk sources this same function directly (rather than keeping a local copy), so the report and the pipeline never drift apart on this logic.

#### Code

```{r}
#| label: src-targets-step-x
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| code-summary: "_targets.R -- x. National + paddock mean diagnostics"

  # x. National + paddock mean diagnostics ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  # National mean time series per raw GPP source -- report-only (gpp_processing.qmd), computed once here rather than at render time. Each raw source's own monthly view reuses its own already-loaded-and-clamped composite target (composite_gpp_rast_modis/composite_gpp_rast_viirs_*) via finish_gpp_period_raster() -- rebuilding this from raw files via build_gpp_period_raster()'s one-shot wrapper instead would silently re-run load_and_clamp_gpp_composites() over the full raw MOD17 archive a second (and, at paddock grain below, third) time; confirmed live as the dominant cost behind gpp_modis_national_mean/gpp_modis_paddock_mean each taking ~2.5h (see r/b_build_gpp_period_raster.R).
  gpp_modis_national_mean = raster_mean_series(finish_gpp_period_raster(composite_gpp_rast_modis, aus_shp, summarise_by = "month")),
  gpp_viirs_gf_national_mean = raster_mean_series(finish_gpp_period_raster(composite_gpp_rast_viirs_gf, aus_shp, summarise_by = "month")),
  gpp_viirs_nongf_national_mean = raster_mean_series(finish_gpp_period_raster(composite_gpp_rast_viirs_nongf, aus_shp, summarise_by = "month")),

  # Paddock-level counterpart to the national means above (extracted at structured-survey paddock points, not averaged nationally) -- report-only, gpp_processing.qmd. See r/b_build_gpp_pixel_ratio_raster.R for why national and paddock means can disagree here.
  gpp_pml_paddock_mean = raster_mean_series(pml_gpp_rast, structured_survey_points),
  gpp_modis_paddock_mean = raster_mean_series(finish_gpp_period_raster(composite_gpp_rast_modis, aus_shp, summarise_by = "month"), structured_survey_points),
  gpp_viirs_gf_paddock_mean = raster_mean_series(finish_gpp_period_raster(composite_gpp_rast_viirs_gf, aus_shp, summarise_by = "month"), structured_survey_points),
  gpp_viirs_nongf_paddock_mean = raster_mean_series(finish_gpp_period_raster(composite_gpp_rast_viirs_nongf, aus_shp, summarise_by = "month"), structured_survey_points),
  gpp_corrected_paddock_mean = raster_mean_series(gpp_raster_coarse, structured_survey_points),

  # GPP-specific source/splice/correction methodology, rendered here (not section 6/7) since it documents exactly the record just built above -- see r/b_download_pml_data.R onward.
  # working_directory pinned to "quarto_reports" -- tar_quarto()'s own default (unset) forces
  # execute_dir = getwd() at the point this command is built, i.e. project root under tar_make(),
  # overriding quarto::quarto_render()'s own real default (the document's own directory), which a
  # manual `quarto render` of this file uses instead. gpp_processing.qmd's own #| file: "../r/..."
  # chunk options resolve relative to execute_dir, not the document's own location: those chunks
  # read fine under manual render (execute_dir defaults to quarto_reports/ there) but break under
  # tar_make() specifically once execute_dir is forced to project root instead ("../r/..." from
  # project root doesn't exist). Pinning working_directory here keeps execute_dir consistently
  # quarto_reports/ either way.
  tar_quarto(gpp_processing_html, path = "quarto_reports/gpp_processing.qmd", working_directory = "quarto_reports", quiet = TRUE),
```

### xi. Fine-scale, focal-smoothed GPP

The one exception to "coarse, landscape-scale" (see Overview above): I build a native-resolution, focal-smoothed GPP layer from `monthly_gpp_rast` (not the PML-spliced, 0.1°-resampled `gpp_raster_coarse`), originally built only as a *detection* covariate for rapid assessment's own active burrow counts (ground cover can obscure a burrow at the exact survey transect), and, since 2026-09, also a core predictor in `chewcard_count_exploration.qmd` (Section D), which needs it for every state including WA. `compute_focal_raster()` (r/b_compute_focal_raster.R) does the smoothing itself -- a 3x3-cell window average, also filling a masked cell from its own valid neighbours (`na.policy = "all"`) rather than leaving it NA, provided at least one neighbour has data. @fig-gpp-paddock-timeseries below shows broadscale vs. fine-scale GPP over time at real paddocks.

```{r}
#| label: fig-gpp-paddock-timeseries
#| fig-cap: "Broadscale (0.1°, red) and fine-scale (focal-smoothed, blue) GPP over time at three real, long-term live-trap paddocks, one per AE zone (Mallee, SA Mid North and NSW-Vic Slopes). Fine-scale only exists from 2000 (MODIS start); where both exist they track closely, with fine-scale sometimes pulling below broadscale at a sharp local peak -- the same focal-smoothing effect visible over time rather than spatially."
#| fig-asp: 0.85

# Three long-term live-trap paddocks, one per AE zone for geographic spread: the longest-running
# still-active trap paddock in each of the three zones with the longest trap history. Named
# directly rather than chosen from the survey data, so this GPP report depends only
# on GPP targets and isn't re-rendered by unrelated survey-data or cleaning changes.
demo_paddock_ids <- c(2288853, 4056644, 1231334)

demo_paddocks <- paddocks_sf_with_soil_type |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  dplyr::filter(paddock_id %in% demo_paddock_ids) |>
  dplyr::transmute(paddock_id, longitude = longitude_paddock, latitude = latitude_paddock, ae_zone, state) |>
  # Keep the order above (longest trap history first) for the facets.
  dplyr::arrange(match(paddock_id, demo_paddock_ids)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(paddock_label = sprintf("Paddock %s (%s, %s)", paddock_id, ae_zone, state))

# raster_mean_series() always collapses multiple points into one shared mean (its usual national-
# vs-paddock-mean use throughout this report) -- called once per paddock here instead (via pmap),
# so each paddock keeps its own separate series rather than being averaged together.
broad_series <- purrr::pmap_dfr(demo_paddocks, function(paddock_id, longitude, latitude, paddock_label, ...) {
  raster_mean_series(gpp_raster_coarse, data.frame(longitude = longitude, latitude = latitude)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(paddock_label = paddock_label, source = "Broadscale (0.1°, gpp_raster_coarse)")
})
fine_series <- purrr::pmap_dfr(demo_paddocks, function(paddock_id, longitude, latitude, paddock_label, ...) {
  raster_mean_series(gpp_focal_raster, data.frame(longitude = longitude, latitude = latitude)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(paddock_label = paddock_label, source = "Fine-scale (focal-smoothed, gpp_focal_raster)")
})
gpp_series <- dplyr::bind_rows(broad_series, fine_series) |>
  dplyr::mutate(paddock_label = factor(paddock_label, levels = demo_paddocks$paddock_label))

ggplot(gpp_series, aes(date, value, colour = source)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~paddock_label, ncol = 1) + # fixed y (default) -- one shared GPP scale across all three paddocks, so relative productivity between them is directly comparable (found via user review, 2026-09; supersedes an earlier free_y version)
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1", name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "GPP (gC/m²/day)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Correction and Splice Diagnostics {#sec-gpp-figures}

### Cross-product bias-check diagnostics (steps iii., ix.)

```{r}
#| label: fig-agreement-by-month
#| fig-cap: "Agreement by calendar month for the three product pairs this pipeline bias-corrects: correlation (left) and bias (right), one row per comparison -- (a) gap-filled vs non-gap-filled VIIRS, (b) MOD17 vs VNP17, (c) PML-V2 vs this pipeline's own NASA record. Line/points are the across-year mean, ribbon the full range, dashed line zero bias. Each column shares one y-scale across all three rows, so the bias panels show real relative magnitude: PML's own bias runs roughly 10x wider across the year than either NASA-internal comparison's, peaking in late winter/spring. Correlation stays consistently strong (0.8-0.9ish) throughout for all three -- PML's swing is a real seasonal shift in level, not a breakdown in agreement."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-asp: 0.9

# One row per calendar month x metric -- across-year mean (the line) and
# min/max (the ribbon) of that metric restricted to that one calendar month,
# pooling every period of overlap. A plain chronological plot (one point per
# period) shows the long-run picture but buries any within-year (seasonal)
# shape in however much noise -- this collapses the year dimension instead,
# since the ratio correction below is itself computed per calendar month, not
# just per pixel, so the seasonal shape is the one that actually matters for
# validating that design. period is grain-neutral (compare_gpp_rasters()'s
# own column, 2026-08) -- a plain composite date ("2013-06-10") for a
# composite-grain comparison (GF/NGF, MOD17/VNP17), or "<month>_<year>" for
# a monthly-grain one (PML/NASA) -- so month extraction has to handle both
# conventions.
period_to_month <- function(period) {
  ifelse(grepl("-", period), lubridate::month(as.Date(period)), as.integer(sub("_.*", "", period)))
}
gpp_bias_by_month <- function(bias_check_df, var) {
  bias_check_df |>
    dplyr::mutate(month = period_to_month(period)) |>
    dplyr::group_by(month) |>
    dplyr::summarise(avg = mean(.data[[var]]), lo = min(.data[[var]]), hi = max(.data[[var]]), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::mutate(month_label = factor(month.abb[month], levels = month.abb))
}

# One combined figure (2026-09, was three separate ones -- one per product pair -- folded into one
# grid instead, since they're the same plot grammar applied to three different comparisons). Every
# row uses the same black line/grey ribbon rather than each keeping its own former per-figure
# colour (green/orange/brown) -- confirmed live those distinct colours read as a categorical
# distinction that didn't need making, since the row labels already say which comparison is which
# (found via user review, 2026-09).
#
# Two columns (correlation, bias), one row per comparison, both columns sharing one y-scale down
# their own 3 rows -- NOT free per row/panel (found via user review, 2026-09, superseding an
# earlier free-per-panel version). ggplot2's own facet_grid(rows ~ cols, scales = "free_y") ties
# scale-freeing to whichever variable is on ROWS, not columns (confirmed live: a minimal repro with
# facet_grid(row ~ col, scales = "free_y") shares one y-range across BOTH columns within a row, the
# opposite of what's needed here) -- so a single facet_grid(comparison ~ series) call can't give
# "shared per column" with comparison as rows. Building each metric as its own single-column
# facet_grid(comparison ~ .) instead -- one shared scale down its own 3 rows, by construction, since
# there's only one column -- and combining the two side by side via patchwork gets both a genuine
# per-column shared scale AND comparison-as-rows/metric-as-columns labelling.
comparison_levels <- c("a) Gap-filled vs non-gap-filled VIIRS", "b) MOD17 vs VNP17", "c) PML-V2 vs NASA")

correlation_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  gpp_bias_by_month(gpp_gf_bias_check, "correlation")    |> dplyr::mutate(comparison = comparison_levels[1]),
  gpp_bias_by_month(gpp_modis_bias_check, "correlation") |> dplyr::mutate(comparison = comparison_levels[2]),
  gpp_bias_by_month(gpp_pml_bias_check, "correlation")   |> dplyr::mutate(comparison = comparison_levels[3])
) |> dplyr::mutate(comparison = factor(comparison, levels = comparison_levels))

bias_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  gpp_bias_by_month(gpp_gf_bias_check, "bias_mean")    |> dplyr::mutate(comparison = comparison_levels[1]),
  gpp_bias_by_month(gpp_modis_bias_check, "bias_mean") |> dplyr::mutate(comparison = comparison_levels[2]),
  gpp_bias_by_month(gpp_pml_bias_check, "bias_mean")   |> dplyr::mutate(comparison = comparison_levels[3])
) |> dplyr::mutate(comparison = factor(comparison, levels = comparison_levels))

p_corr <- ggplot(correlation_df, aes(month_label, avg, group = 1)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey60", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = "black", size = 1.5) +
  # facet_wrap(), not facet_grid() -- facet_grid()'s own row strip sits on the panel's right edge
  # (previously shown between the two columns, on p_corr's own side only, to avoid repeating it);
  # facet_wrap()'s own strip draws ABOVE each panel by default instead, which is what's wanted here
  # -- and since comparison is still the only faceting variable, ncol = 1 still stacks the three
  # comparisons in one column with one shared y-scale down all three, same as facet_grid(comparison
  # ~ .) already gave (found via user review, 2026-09: preferred a repeated above-panel label over
  # a single shared side one).
  facet_wrap(~comparison, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Correlation") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11))

p_bias <- ggplot(bias_df, aes(month_label, avg, group = 1)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey60", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = "black", size = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap(~comparison, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Bias (gC/m²/day)") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11))

p_corr + p_bias
```

### Pixel-scale corrections and splice (steps iv.-vi., ix.)

```{r}
#| label: fig-pixel-ratio-maps
#| fig-cap: "MOD17 (a-c), VIIRS non-gap-filled/gap-filled (d-f) and PML-V2 (g-i) pixel-scale corrections, each at its own most representative date (MOD17: 2013-07-11; NGF/GF: most recent shared composite; PML-V2: August 1995, its largest-bias month). All three share one level scale (a/c/d/f/g/i, gC/m²/day) and one ratio scale (b/e/h). Both corrections are spatially coherent: MOD17 (b) is scaled up almost everywhere, since VNP17 reads systematically higher; PML (h) is scaled down hardest exactly where raw PML ran hottest (g vs i)."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-asp: 0.85

## fig-asp lowered from 1.25 -- that value was tuned for legend.position = "right" (a vertical
## colorbar, using width rather than height); once the legends moved to "bottom" (found via user
## review, 2026-09) the same 1.25 left a large blank margin above the panels. 0.85 confirmed live
## as a good fit for the horizontal-legend layout.

# "2013-07-11" (roughly midway through MOD17/VNP17's real 2012+ overlap) is not itself an exact
# 8-day composite date, so snap to the nearest one actually present as a layer name -- the same
# nearest-available-date approach as gf_demo_date below, just by proximity instead of by shared max.
modis_demo_date <- names(composite_gpp_rast_modis)[
  which.min(abs(as.Date(names(composite_gpp_rast_modis)) - as.Date("2013-07-11")))
]
modis_before <- composite_gpp_rast_modis[[modis_demo_date]]; names(modis_before) <- "value"
modis_after  <- composite_gpp_rast_modis_corrected[[modis_demo_date]]; names(modis_after) <- "value"
modis_ratio  <- gpp_modis_pixel_ratio_rast[[as.character(lubridate::month(as.Date(modis_demo_date)))]]; names(modis_ratio) <- "value"

gf_demo_date <- max(intersect(names(composite_gpp_rast_viirs_gf), names(composite_gpp_rast_viirs_nongf))) # most recent composite both GF and NGF actually share
gf_before <- composite_gpp_rast_viirs_nongf[[gf_demo_date]]; names(gf_before) <- "value"
gf_after  <- composite_gpp_rast_viirs_nongf_corrected[[gf_demo_date]]; names(gf_after) <- "value"
gf_ratio  <- gpp_gf_pixel_ratio_rast[[as.character(lubridate::month(as.Date(gf_demo_date)))]]; names(gf_ratio) <- "value"

# PML-V2's own demo date -- August 1995, the month with the largest PML/NASA bias (fig-agreement-
# by-month above), same date this used to be shown on its own in fig-pml-pixel-ratio-map before
# that figure was folded into this one (2026-09, combining fig-pixel-ratio-maps and
# fig-pml-pixel-ratio-map into one nine-panel figure -- both are the same before/ratio/after map
# grammar applied to a different product, and PML's own ratio_range already matched MOD17/VIIRS's
# exactly (0.4-2.5) even before this merge, so a single shared scale pair costs nothing in
# precision). PML-V2 is already on the same 0.1 degree grid/gC/m²/day unit as the others, so pools
# straight into the same level_range/ratio_scale below with no extra reconciling.
pml_demo_date <- "8_1995"
pml_before <- pml_gpp_rast[[pml_demo_date]]; names(pml_before) <- "value"
pml_after  <- pml_gpp_rast_corrected[[pml_demo_date]]; names(pml_after) <- "value"
pml_ratio  <- gpp_pml_pixel_ratio_rast[["8"]]; names(pml_ratio) <- "value"

# Downsampled (~500m native -> ~4.6km, fact = 10, mean aggregation) before converting to a data
# frame -- this figure's whole point is the correction's national-scale spatial PATTERN, which a
# ~4.6km cell still shows just as clearly as a ~500m one at this document's own national-map
# display size. as.data.frame(xy = TRUE) on 6 full-resolution national layers (~39.2M cells each)
# was this report's single most expensive figure (~8-15 min, confirmed live) -- aggregating first
# cuts that cell count, and so the conversion/plotting cost, by ~100x (2026-09, found via user
# review). Done before level_range's own quantile below too, not just before plotting, so that
# computation is cheap as well -- a 98th percentile over ~100x fewer cells is indistinguishable at
# this figure's own display precision.
#
# PML-V2 does NOT get the same fact = 10 treatment -- confirmed live PML-V2's own native grid is
# already 0.1 degree (74,028 cells/layer nationally, vs MOD17/VIIRS's ~39.2M), so the same factor
# that turns MOD17/VIIRS's ~500m cells into a still-fine ~4.6km would instead coarsen PML's own
# already-coarse ~11km cells down to ~110km -- a real, unintended loss of PML's own native detail,
# not a "consistent display resolution" the way an earlier version of this comment claimed (that
# reasoning had it backwards: matching factors doesn't mean matching output resolution when the
# two inputs start at very different native resolutions). PML-V2's own 74,028 cells were always
# cheap enough for as.data.frame() with no downsampling needed at all (found via user review,
# 2026-09).
agg <- function(r) terra::aggregate(r, fact = 10, fun = "mean", na.rm = TRUE)
modis_before <- agg(modis_before); modis_after <- agg(modis_after); modis_ratio <- agg(modis_ratio)
gf_before    <- agg(gf_before);    gf_after    <- agg(gf_after);    gf_ratio    <- agg(gf_ratio)

# One shared level scale across all six level panels (capped at the 98th percentile pooled across
# all six, not the raw max, so a handful of extreme pixels don't wash out the real variation
# everywhere else) -- valid because MODIS, VIIRS and PML-V2 are all already the same unit (see
# comment above), unlike an arbitrary shared axis across different quantities.
level_range <- c(0, stats::quantile(c(terra::values(modis_before), terra::values(modis_after),
                                       terra::values(gf_before), terra::values(gf_after),
                                       terra::values(pml_before), terra::values(pml_after)),
                                     0.98, na.rm = TRUE))
level_scale <- scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "GPP (gC/m²/day)", option = "C", limits = level_range, oob = scales::squish)
# Diverging, centred on 1 (no correction) -- a ratio has a genuine reference point (1 = unchanged),
# unlike a plain magnitude, so red/blue (below/above 1) reads directly as "scaled down"/"scaled up"
# at a glance, which a sequential palette (an earlier version of this figure) can't show.
ratio_range <- c(0.4, 2.5)
ratio_scale <- scale_fill_distiller(name = "Correction ratio (target ÷ source)", palette = "RdBu", direction = 1, limits = ratio_range, oob = scales::squish)

to_df <- function(r, panel) as.data.frame(r, xy = TRUE) |> dplyr::mutate(panel = panel)
mk_panel <- function(df, scale_obj, title) {
  # geom_raster(), not geom_tile() -- geom_tile() draws every cell as its own polygon, which is
  # fast enough for the small native-scale crop in fig-gpp-masking-coastal-detail above but far
  # too slow at these two figures' own national extent (confirmed live: geom_tile() took several
  # minutes per figure and was killed before finishing). geom_raster() blits a single bitmap
  # instead and is orders of magnitude faster; its own "pixels placed at uneven intervals" warning
  # is a sub-pixel rounding concern in these rasters' own grid, invisible at a national map's
  # actual display scale, so accepted here rather than paying geom_tile()'s real cost to avoid it.
  ggplot(df, aes(x, y, fill = value)) +
    geom_raster() +
    coord_equal() +
    scale_obj +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = title) +
    theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.title = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5))
}

p1 <- mk_panel(to_df(modis_before, "Raw MOD17 (uncorrected)"), level_scale, "Raw MOD17 (uncorrected)")
p2 <- mk_panel(to_df(modis_ratio, "Ratio applied"), ratio_scale, "Ratio applied")
p3 <- mk_panel(to_df(modis_after, "Corrected MOD17"), level_scale, "Corrected MOD17")

q1 <- mk_panel(to_df(gf_before, "Raw non-gap-filled (uncorrected)"), level_scale, "Raw non-gap-filled (uncorrected)")
q2 <- mk_panel(to_df(gf_ratio, "Ratio applied"), ratio_scale, "Ratio applied")
q3 <- mk_panel(to_df(gf_after, "Corrected non-gap-filled"), level_scale, "Corrected non-gap-filled")

r1 <- mk_panel(to_df(pml_before, "Raw PML (uncorrected)"), level_scale, "Raw PML (uncorrected)")
r2 <- mk_panel(to_df(pml_ratio, "Ratio applied"), ratio_scale, "Ratio applied")
r3 <- mk_panel(to_df(pml_after, "Corrected PML"), level_scale, "Corrected PML")

# One flat, nine-panel patchwork -- byrow = FALSE fills column-major (a-c down the MODIS column,
# d-f down the GF column, g-i down the PML column), and guides = "collect" applies globally rather
# than per-column, so the six identical level_scale panels merge into one legend and the three
# identical ratio_scale panels merge into another -- 2 legends total instead of 9, since all three
# corrections share their scales (see caption above). plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
# tags all nine leaf panels in drawing order.
p1 + p2 + p3 + q1 + q2 + q3 + r1 + r2 + r3 +
  patchwork::plot_layout(ncol = 3, byrow = FALSE, guides = "collect") +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-splice-continuity
#| fig-cap: "Raw (uncorrected) source vs. the pipeline's output at each of the three splice boundaries, zoomed to that boundary's own window -- exactly where a real correction problem would show up -- at both national mean (left) and structured-survey paddocks (right, the grain the forecast model actually reads). (a) PML's pre-2000/2000+ boundary: raw PML carries a systematic offset the correction removes, and the pipeline output switches source entirely at 2000. (b) MOD17's 2011/2012 handoff to VIIRS: raw MOD17 sits off the pipeline output before correction pulls it into line, then VIIRS takes over. (c) VIIRS's near-real-time boundary: gap-filled composites blend with a corrected non-gap-filled fallback -- the two lines stay close throughout."
#| fig-asp: 1

# This figure used to be two separate ones -- fig-gpp-all-sources (raw vs. pipeline output,
# paddock grain, each source's own full window) and this figure at national grain only, zoomed to
# each boundary -- merged into one (2026-09, found via user review) once both were confirmed to be
# checking the same underlying question (does raw line up with the pipeline's corrected output?),
# just split across grain and zoom in a way that read as redundant rather than complementary. This
# version keeps the more informative zoom (a boundary is exactly where a real problem would show
# up) and adds paddock grain as a second facet column instead of a whole separate figure.
#
# Panel labels defined once as variables, not repeated string literals.
national_grain_label <- "a) National mean"
paddock_grain_label  <- "b) At survey paddocks"
grain_levels <- c(national_grain_label, paddock_grain_label)

# pml_gpp_rast is now itself masked to covariate_download_region's own polygon
# and to aus_shp's coastline (_targets.R's own "viii. Crop PML to same area",
# 2026-09 fix) -- the same two masks A) NASA's own finished record uses in
# vi. above -- so this crop is no longer working around a missing mask.
# The two extents can still differ slightly, though: resample_to_grid() crops
# monthly_gpp_rast_coarse down to covariate_download_region's own footprint
# independently (_targets.R's own "ix. Bias-check, correct and splice in
# PML") -- crop pml_gpp_rast down to that same extent here too, so this
# raw-vs-pipeline-output national mean is comparing the same pixels on both
# sides. Reused as-is by fig-splice-continuity below, so this crop only
# happens once.
pml_gpp_rast_study_area <- terra::crop(pml_gpp_rast, monthly_gpp_rast_coarse)

all_sources_national_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  # pml_gpp_rast_study_area (above), not raw pml_gpp_rast directly -- see that variable's own
  # comment. gpp_modis_national_mean/gpp_viirs_*_national_mean don't need the same fix -- they're
  # already built via finish_gpp_period_raster(), which masks to aus_shp (and was downloaded at
  # covariate_download_region's own polygon extent to begin with).
  raster_mean_series(pml_gpp_rast_study_area) |> dplyr::mutate(source = "PML-V2 (raw)"),
  gpp_modis_national_mean          |> dplyr::mutate(source = "MODIS (raw)"),
  gpp_viirs_gf_national_mean       |> dplyr::mutate(source = "VIIRS gap-filled (raw)"),
  gpp_viirs_nongf_national_mean    |> dplyr::mutate(source = "VIIRS non-gap-filled (raw)")
) |> dplyr::mutate(grain = national_grain_label)

all_sources_paddock_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  gpp_pml_paddock_mean         |> dplyr::mutate(source = "PML-V2 (raw)"),
  gpp_modis_paddock_mean       |> dplyr::mutate(source = "MODIS (raw)"),
  gpp_viirs_gf_paddock_mean    |> dplyr::mutate(source = "VIIRS gap-filled (raw)"),
  gpp_viirs_nongf_paddock_mean |> dplyr::mutate(source = "VIIRS non-gap-filled (raw)")
) |> dplyr::mutate(grain = paddock_grain_label)

all_sources_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(all_sources_national_df, all_sources_paddock_df) |>
  dplyr::mutate(grain = factor(grain, levels = grain_levels))

pipeline_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  gpp_monthly_df             |> dplyr::mutate(grain = national_grain_label),
  gpp_corrected_paddock_mean |> dplyr::mutate(grain = paddock_grain_label)
) |> dplyr::mutate(grain = factor(grain, levels = grain_levels))

raw_role      <- "Raw (uncorrected)"
pipeline_role <- "Pipeline output (corrected/spliced)"

# gpp_corrected_paddock_mean has no "source" column of its own -- replicated once per raw source
# here so build_splice_window_df() below can filter it down by source the same way it filters the
# raw dataframes, rather than as an implicit "no facet column = draw in every panel" side effect (a
# real but easy-to-miss ggplot2 behaviour).
pipeline_paddock_full_df <- purrr::map_dfr(unique(all_sources_paddock_df$source), function(s) {
  dplyr::mutate(gpp_corrected_paddock_mean, source = s)
})

# Panel labels defined once as variables, not repeated string literals, so the tags stay consistent
# everywhere the same facet value needs to be written (the data build below, and vline_df's own
# restriction to just the PML/MODIS rows) -- same pattern national_grain_label/paddock_grain_label
# above uses for its own a)/b) tags.
pml_splice_label    <- "a) PML pre-2000/2000+ splice"
modis_splice_label  <- "b) MOD17/VIIRS 2011/2012 handoff"
gf_splice_label      <- "c) VIIRS near-real-time splice"
splice_levels <- c(pml_splice_label, modis_splice_label, gf_splice_label)

# One boundary's worth of raw-vs-pipeline data, at BOTH grains -- avoids repeating the same
# national+paddock, raw+pipeline assembly three times over (once per boundary below). Comparing
# against RAW (uncorrected) MOD17/PML/VIIRS, not each source's own corrected version, is also the
# more informative version of this check: corrected data matching the pipeline output mostly just
# re-validates the splice/aggregation code ran consistently twice, whereas raw data visibly pulling
# onto the pipeline's own level right at the boundary is the actual bias-correction claim this
# figure exists to support. Filters by exact calendar years (window_years) for the PML/MODIS
# boundaries, which sit at a fixed date; the VIIRS boundary is a moving target instead, so it's
# filtered by the raw non-gap-filled data's own real date range (date_range) rather than a
# hand-picked year window.
build_splice_window_df <- function(source_label, correction_label, window_years = NULL, date_range = NULL) {
  in_window <- function(df) {
    if (!is.null(window_years)) dplyr::filter(df, lubridate::year(date) %in% window_years)
    else dplyr::filter(df, date >= date_range[1], date <= date_range[2])
  }
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    in_window(dplyr::filter(all_sources_national_df, source == source_label)) |>
      dplyr::transmute(date, value, grain = national_grain_label, role = raw_role),
    in_window(dplyr::filter(all_sources_paddock_df, source == source_label)) |>
      dplyr::transmute(date, value, grain = paddock_grain_label, role = raw_role),
    in_window(dplyr::filter(pipeline_df, grain == national_grain_label)) |>
      dplyr::transmute(date, value, grain = national_grain_label, role = pipeline_role),
    in_window(dplyr::filter(pipeline_paddock_full_df, source == source_label)) |>
      dplyr::transmute(date, value, grain = paddock_grain_label, role = pipeline_role)
  ) |> dplyr::mutate(correction = correction_label)
}

pml_df <- build_splice_window_df("PML-V2 (raw)", pml_splice_label, window_years = 1996:2004)
modis_df <- build_splice_window_df("MODIS (raw)", modis_splice_label, window_years = 2009:2014)

## gpp_viirs_nongf_national_mean (and so all_sources_national_df's own VIIRS non-gap-filled rows)
## already only spans the window where a non-gap-filled fallback is actually needed, so that's used
## as the real date range here rather than a hand-picked year window.
nongf_window <- range(dplyr::filter(all_sources_national_df, source == "VIIRS non-gap-filled (raw)")$date)
gf_df <- build_splice_window_df("VIIRS non-gap-filled (raw)", gf_splice_label, date_range = nongf_window)

splice_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(pml_df, modis_df, gf_df) |>
  dplyr::mutate(correction = factor(correction, levels = splice_levels), grain = factor(grain, levels = grain_levels))

# Marker lines, restricted to just the PML/MODIS rows -- VIIRS's own boundary is a moving target,
# not one fixed date, so it gets no equivalent marker.
vline_df <- tibble::tibble(
  correction = factor(c(pml_splice_label, modis_splice_label), levels = splice_levels),
  xdate = as.Date(c("2000-01-01", "2012-01-01"))
)

# Two separately-faceted single-column plots combined via patchwork, same construction as
# fig-agreement-by-month above -- not one facet_grid(correction ~ grain) call -- for two reasons
# (found via user review, 2026-09). First, labelling: facet_grid()'s own row strip sits on the
# panel's right edge, whereas facet_wrap()'s own strip draws ABOVE each panel, matching
# fig-agreement-by-month's own row-label convention. Second, and more binding here: facet_grid()
# can only free a scale per ROW or per COLUMN (grid()'s own scales = "free" still shares an axis
# across every panel in the same row/column, confirmed live -- see fig-agreement-by-month's own
# header for the same finding applied to y alone), never per INDIVIDUAL panel -- but this figure's
# 6 panels each need their own independent x AND y range (three boundaries at very different dates,
# two grains at very different GPP magnitudes), which only facet_wrap()'s own scales = "free" gives.
p_national <- ggplot(dplyr::filter(splice_df, grain == national_grain_label), aes(date, value, colour = role)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(data = vline_df, aes(xintercept = xdate), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  facet_wrap(~correction, ncol = 1, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "GPP (gC/m²/day)", colour = NULL, title = national_grain_label) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11))

p_paddock <- ggplot(dplyr::filter(splice_df, grain == paddock_grain_label), aes(date, value, colour = role)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(data = vline_df, aes(xintercept = xdate), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  facet_wrap(~correction, ncol = 1, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL, title = paddock_grain_label) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11))

# guides = "collect" merges both plots' identical role/colour legend into one, placed via the
# outer theme() below (the "&" operator applies to every subplot, not just the last one -- unlike
# "+") -- same pattern fig-pixel-ratio-maps above uses to merge its own repeated per-panel legends.
p_national + p_paddock + patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
